subject: Contract end-stage mechanics: auto-renew cadence & off-ramp notice
messages:
From: Maya Lang <maya.lang@altairsys.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@altairsys.com, Ryan Foster <ryan.foster@altairlegal.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Altair redlines: proposed off-ramp window and auto-renew language

Kim — attaching our redline of the MSA and a short note on the order form. Two items we need to confirm before legal can sign off: 

1) Off-ramp timing: we proposed a 90-day notice rather than 60 to allow internal migration windows; this is in MSA, Section 6.2 (Termination for convenience).
2) Auto-renew cadence: procurement needs the renewal to be annual by default rather than monthly, with an explicit opt-out window of 60 days prior to renewal.

I'm copying Ryan from Altair Legal — he flagged a concern that the current transitional-support language is too vague and may create a de facto obligation. We can make a more prescriptive handover clause if Redwood requires shorter notice.

Attachments: Altair_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline), OrderForm_APX-4821_v2.pdf (proposed commercial changes)

Thanks,
Maya Lang
Head of Procurement, Altair Systems
maya.lang@altairsys.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Lang <maya.lang@altairsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Altair redlines: proposed off-ramp window and auto-renew language

Thanks Maya — received and reviewed quickly with the commercial team. High level notes: 

- 90-day notice: acceptable from a commercial standpoint if we can keep termination-for-convenience cap at 2x monthly committed spend for transition support; otherwise 60 days is our standard.
- Annual auto-renew: Redwoods' default hosting bundles are priced on annual commitments; we can support annual auto-renew, but we need to preserve a 60-day opt-out for enterprise pilots (we typically make pilots a 30–60 day exception).
- Transitional support: we agree with Ryan that the language needs more specificity. Suggest adding a defined "handover period" (30 days) with clear deliverables and a cap on hours.

Requesting legal review from Karthik — can you propose redline language that balances Altair's request for a longer notice window with Redwood's need to limit open-ended support obligations? Ben — leaving commercial on this for pricing impact.

Next steps:
- Karthik to propose targeted redline for Sections 6.1–6.4.
- Ben to confirm cap / fee language for transitional support by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Lang <maya.lang@altairsys.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Altair redlines: proposed off-ramp window and auto-renew language

Maya / Kim — quick commercial input. We can accept a 90-day notice window only if we adjust the off-ramp economics to account for longer reservation of capacity. Proposed compromise: 

- If customer gives 90-day termination for convenience, Redwood will provide a 30-day paid transition package (up to X hours) included; additional support billed at agreed hourly SOW rate.
- Termination cap: 2x monthly committed spend OR a calculator based on average trailing 3-month usage, whichever is higher.
- Auto-renew: set to annual unless the customer signs a pilot addendum marking the agreement as "Pilot — 90 day term". Opt-out window: 60 days prior to renewal.

If Altair needs a longer handover (beyond 30 days), propose we set a defined SOW so expectations and cost are clear. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Lang <maya.lang@altairsys.com>, Ryan Foster <ryan.foster@altairlegal.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Altair redlines: proposed off-ramp window and auto-renew language

Maya / Ryan — thanks for the draft. Attached is a focused redline that: 

- Retains Altair's 90-day notice request for termination for convenience, but adds a defined "Handover Period" of 30 days with a maximum of 120 reimbursable engineering hours unless a separate SOW is executed.
- Caps the termination-for-convenience liability at the greater of (a) two months' committed recurring fees, or (b) an amount equal to the average monthly spend over the prior three months, to avoid under-indexing for consumption spikes.
- Changes auto-renew default to annual with explicit opt-out notice window of 60 days. To accommodate pilots, added an express pilot addendum option that allows shorter notice and pro-rated termination.

Please see attached: Altair_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline with inline comments) and OrderForm_APX-4821_v2.pdf (commercial markup). I attempted to keep language prescriptive (specific deliverables during handover) and introduced a mutual escalation path if there is a dispute about hours. 

If Altair confirms the above, we can prepare final clean MSA and order form for signature and provide a draft SOW template for handover work.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
